findings.subject: 8080/tcp
findings.title: Port 8080 is already in use
findings.description: Service "orders-api" publishes port 8080/tcp on every host address, and that binding is already held on this host by python3 (pid 1767088), listening on port 8080/tcp on 0.0.0.0.
findings.why_it_matters: The container will fail to start: the engine cannot bind a port another process already holds. On a deployment that stops the old stack first, the failure lands after the old one is already down.
findings.what_to_do: Publish a different host port for "orders-api", or stop whatever currently holds 8080 before deploying.

evidence.output: ports: publishes host port 8080/tcp on every host address → container port 80

findings.subject: docker
findings.title: docker is installed but did not answer
findings.description: The docker binary is present, but querying the engine failed: docker is installed but its daemon could not be queried (docker exited 1: failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///nonexistent/docker.sock; check if the path is correct and if the daemon is running: dial unix /nonexistent/docker.sock: connect: no such…); the container, network, volume and image lists are unknown rather than empty. The usual cause is an unprivileged audit: /var/run/docker.sock is readable by root and the docker group only — re-run as root, or as a member of that group, for the container checks. Every check that compares the manifest against existing containers, networks, volumes and images was therefore skipped.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the honesty case that matters most in this section: with the engine unreachable, an empty conflict list means nothing was looked at, not that nothing is in the way.
findings.what_to_do: Re-run the audit as a user who can reach the engine socket (root, or a member of the docker group) to get the conflict checks.

evidence.output: docker is installed but its daemon could not be queried (docker exited 1: failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///nonexistent/docker.sock; check if the path is correct and if the daemon is running: dial unix /nonexistent/docker.sock: connect: no such…); the container, network, volume and image lists are unknown rather than empty. The usual cause is an unprivileged audit: /var/run/docker.sock is readable by root and the docker group only — re-run as root, or as a member of that group, for the container checks

findings.subject: nginx:1.27-alpine
findings.title: Image nginx:1.27-alpine is pinned by tag, not by digest
findings.description: Service "orders-api" uses tag "1.27-alpine", which names a moving target rather than one image.
findings.why_it_matters: A tag can be moved. That makes the deployment unreproducible in the direction that matters: rolling back to "the version that worked" pulls whatever the tag points at today, and two hosts deployed a week apart from the same file are not running the same software.
findings.what_to_do: Pin nginx by digest (image@sha256:…) once you have the version you want.

findings.title: Registry reachability was not checked
findings.description: The deployment pulls from docker.io. This audit does not open outbound connections unless asked, so whether this host can reach them is unknown.
findings.why_it_matters: A host behind an egress firewall passes every other check in this report and then fails at the pull. This line is here so that outcome is not a surprise.
findings.what_to_do: Re-run with --egress to test reachability, or confirm outbound access to those registries by other means.

findings.subject: 2 of 4 unverified
findings.title: The way back could not be fully verified
findings.description: Nothing in the rollback plan was found to be missing, but part of it could not be checked from inside this host. Unable to verify: proxy-config: whether a copy of the apache configuration under /etc/httpd is kept outside this host cannot be seen from inside it; take one before changing it, since a proxy that fails to start takes every site on this host down, not only the new one; snapshot: whether a hypervisor or provider snapshot of this host exists cannot be seen from inside it — confirm with whoever runs the infrastructure before deploying.
findings.why_it_matters: What this audit cannot see is not evidence that it is absent — nor that it exists. Whether the deployment can be undone in full depends on the items above, which only the people running this host can confirm.
findings.what_to_do: Before deploying: note the image digests currently running, copy the web server configuration somewhere outside this host, and confirm a snapshot or a volume backup exists.
